OpenCray keeps Chat, Skills, Files, and Settings inside one shell, so moving around the app stays simple and your place stays predictable.
Below are the key details for the version installed on this device.
These details come directly from the installed build on this device.
Protected paths and other blocked actions stay unavailable, even in more permissive modes.
Sensitive changes can still pause for review before they run, so approvals stay visible.
Rollback only covers local file checkpoints. Network, command, MCP, and other external side effects may need manual cleanup.
V1 stays focused. Real Termux execution, cloud sync, iOS support, parallel multi-agent execution, and a public marketplace review system are not part of this build.

Reset controls may arm once the exact token matches. Case and spacing must match exactly.
A queued chat action is still waiting for a decision, so both reset controls stay disabled until the shell returns to idle. Approve or deny the pending item in Chat first.
Reset memory clears app-level memory and history stores only.
It does not clear the soul profile, workspace grants, MCP state, telemetry or privacy preferences, or About and Version metadata.
Reset soul clears the personality and soul profile only.

Balanced, calm, and explicit about tradeoffs. Good for day-to-day work when you want clarity first.
More decisive and terse. Best when you want direct implementation guidance and minimal ceremony.
More empathetic and encouraging while still respecting constraints and safety rails.
Base voice: calm, methodical, and transparent about boundaries.
Base voice: concise, execution-first, and optimized for concrete next steps.
Base voice: supportive, slightly warmer, and better for collaborative exploration.
Adjust the two core toggles here, with defaults and local retention kept on the same page.
Defaults: Enable telemetry = Off. Enable privacy guard = On.
Even with telemetry off, OpenCray still keeps local settings, workspace access state, consent choices, and recent audit history on this device until a later clear-data flow removes them.
Default: Off. Turning telemetry off blocks outbound telemetry, but local settings, approvals, and recent audit entries remain stored on this device.
Local redaction stays enabled for eligible analytics and audit details.
Eligible analytics and audit details can use full local detail.
Default: On. Privacy guard changes what later telemetry may include, while local retention still keeps the current setting and recent audit history on-device.
